title: fix(plugin-form): hand a section's `description` to the default layout's divider
body:
Fixes objectui#9779

Clause-②: no

The key is already declared on both sides (`ObjectFormSection.description` in this repo's own `@object-ui/types`, `FormSection.description` in `@objectstack/spec`) and is already rendered by other layout arms, and `SectionDivider` has always drawn one. Making the default layout read it relaxes no accepted set and enlarges no public surface. Re-declared here by me, as the seat asked; I reached the same reading it did, on the declarations above rather than on its say-so.

## What was wrong

`SimpleObjectForm`'s grouped branch — the layout a section-carrying `object-form` gets when it declares no `formType` — rebuilds every section key by key into a virtual `section-divider` row. That rebuild copied `label`, the ADR-0089 predicate, the objectui#6236 membership claim and the collapse pair, and not `description`. So the blurb never reached the divider, while the sibling `label` on the same member did — which is what made the miss invisible to an author.

One key copied onto that push. Nothing else in the renderer moved.

## My own measurement of the arms — the card's table is NOT what I measured

⚠️ I re-measured rather than inheriting the card's list, and the reading differs from it. A throwaway probe mounted the same two sections (each carrying `label` + `description`) through the real `ObjectForm` for every arm, plus `DrawerForm` mounted directly, and read `document.body.textContent`. Probe deleted after measuring; it is not in this diff.

| arm | blurb rendered? | the call it travels through |
|---|---|---|
| default (no `formType`) / `simple` | ⛔ no, **before this PR** | `SimpleObjectForm`'s `section-divider` push — the fix |
| `tabbed` | ✅ yes | ObjectForm's tabbed section map to `TabbedForm`'s `tabGroups`, out as `fieldTabs[].description`, rendered by the form renderer's field-tabs group header |
| `wizard` | ✅ yes (current step only, which is the wizard's whole shape) | ObjectForm's wizard step map, then `FormSectionContainer`'s own `description` prop |
| `split` | ✅ yes | ObjectForm's split map, then `paneFields`' divider push, gated `section.label || section.description` |
| `modal` | ✅ yes | ObjectForm's modal map, then the stacked-sections divider push gated `g.title || g.description` (and `fieldTabs[].description` on the `contentLayout: 'tabbed'` arm) |
| `drawer` | ⛔ **no — and this PR does not change it** | ObjectForm's drawer map copies the key, then `DrawerForm`'s own divider push drops it again |

⇒ it was **two** arms missing the key, not one. `DrawerForm` is deliberately untouched here: the seat's dispatch says not to widen into the other arms, `DrawerForm`'s divider push is a separate site rather than a shared path, and an arm the card asserts is healthy turning out not to be is a finding for the seat to file, not something to fold into a one-arm repair. Handed back in my report.

## The pin moved WITH the fix, and it is shown failing

`objectFormSectionMembers-8071`'s sixth row pinned the drop as behaviour (objectui#8071 slice 11 wrote pins only and handed the drop back as a finding). It is rewritten in this same change onto the new behaviour, with its comment saying what it used to pin and which card changed it. It was ⛔ not weakened and ⛔ not deleted: it is still the only assertion watching this key, and it now reads the blurb off the divider row itself rather than off the form's whole `textContent` — an arrival assertion against `textContent` would be satisfied by the string rendering anywhere at all.

Ablation, run from the committed state so both legs are byte-provable, with a `trap` restoring on any exit:

- HEAD blob of the renderer: `83a8fbd13c44626aeb5097b97847d41ab3ea1b9b`
- mutation = delete the one copied key. Landed on disk, proven by the anchor count going 1 to 0 (⛔ not by the editor's exit code), and by the mutated blob hashing `101ec9230ec6b175c4fd1318a9cfda82fbdfd164`, different from HEAD's.
- mutated leg: `Tests 1 failed | 6 passed (7)`, and the one red is exactly row 6 — `AssertionError: … expected [] to deeply equal [ 'Totals as invoiced' ]`. Every other row, the boundary row included, stayed green.
- restore leg: `git checkout HEAD --` on the file (⛔ not a bare `git checkout --`, which restores from the polluted index). Restored blob `83a8fbd13c44626aeb5097b97847d41ab3ea1b9b` — equal to HEAD's — `git diff HEAD` empty, anchor count back to 1, and the pin green again at `Tests 7 passed (7)`.

No build was needed for either leg and none was used: `*.test.tsx` runs under the root vitest projects, whose alias map redirects every `@object-ui/*` specifier to that package's `src`, so the mutation was read directly. (The dist-pin family is the deliberate exception, and this file is not one of them.)

## What else asserts the old behaviour — swept, two hits, both moved

- Mechanical sweep: the whole `packages/plugin-form` suite at the fixed tree — `Test Files 96 passed (96)`, `Tests 920 passed | 1 skipped (921)`. Nothing else in the package went red, so nothing else in it was asserting the drop.
- Text sweep across the tree for the card's sentinel, and for prose pairing `description` with drop/never-reaches/silently wording: exactly two carriers. Row 6 itself, and the member-pin ledger entry for `object-form.sections` in `registry-inputs-spec-parity`, whose `pins` prose spelled out the LIMIT in words. The ledger prose is not compared mechanically (only the pin file's existence and whether it names the block and the key are), so it would have gone on describing a behaviour that no longer exists — commandment #9's failure mode. Corrected in the same change; that test still passes, `Tests 199 passed (199)`.
- Six further files outside `plugin-form` that mount an `object-form` and mention `description` were read individually: all of them are about a FIELD's description or a form-level one, none asserts a section blurb's absence.

⇒ ⛔ row 6 was not the only carrier, but it was the only *assertion*.

## Changeset grade — measured from a build, not assumed

A changeset is owed and it is a real bump, ⛔ not an empty-frontmatter declaration. `@object-ui/plugin-form` patch.

Measured on the corpus that package's `files` array actually publishes (`dist` plus the three markdown/licence entries), built on this branch after building the dependency closure:

- **The fix reaches it.** The compiled `SimpleObjectForm` divider push in `dist/index.js` — the one carrying `colSpan: 4`, the collapse pair and the `onToggle` closure — now carries `description: r.description`. The source spelling does not survive minification, so the property on the compiled push is the marker, ⛔ not a grep for the source line.
- **Lit control, same corpus:** `section-divider` is present in `dist/index.js`, `dist/index.umd.cjs` and two `.d.ts` files — the corpus is one this grep can see into.
- **Absent control, same corpus:** the pin's sentinel string `Totals as invoiced` appears nowhere in `dist` — the grep can return zero, so the hit above is not a grep that hits everything.
- **Second absent control, same artifact:** three structurally identical divider pushes in the SAME bundle (the drawer arm's two and the modal derived arm's) carry no `description` property at all — so the bundler is not inventing the key, and the property on the fixed site got there from the source change.

## The boundary this PR deliberately did NOT move

The divider row exists only for a member that yields a heading — a `name` or a `label` — which is the "untitled trailing bucket renders flat" rule the file's own comment states and row 3 pins. A member carrying a `description` and neither of those therefore still draws no divider and still drops its blurb, whereas `split` / `modal` / `wizard` / `tabbed` render one for it.

I did not widen that gate, because it decides more than this key: it also gates the ADR-0089 predicate row and the objectui#6236 membership claim, and the collapse pair hangs off the same condition — so a headingless section that gained a divider would newly have its predicate gate its whole group, and a `collapsed: true` on it would newly take its fields out of the DOM. Those are rulings about other keys. The shape is pinned as behaviour in a new row beside row 6 — the same way row 6 recorded the drop — and handed back as a finding.

## Tests

- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-form/src/__tests__/objectFormSectionMembers-8071.test.tsx` — `Tests 7 passed (7)`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run packages/plugin-form/` — `Test Files 96 passed (96)`, `Tests 920 passed | 1 skipped (921)`.
- `pnpm exec vitest run apps/console/src/__tests__/registry-inputs-spec-parity.test.ts` — `Tests 199 passed (199)`.
- `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form type-check` — exit 0; it runs `tsc --noEmit` AND `tsc -p tsconfig.test.json`, so the rewritten pin is type-checked too. The copied key needs no cast: `ObjectFormSection.description` is declared, so a rename would be caught by the compiler.
- `pnpm --filter '@object-ui/plugin-form^...' build` then `pnpm --filter @object-ui/plugin-form build` — both exit 0 (the closure first; the package cannot typecheck its own build against unbuilt dependencies).
- Gates: `check:changeset-presence` (red before the changeset, green after), `check:control-bytes`, `check:new-line-citations` (0 new), `check:changeset-claims`, `check:pending-changeset-literals` — all exit 0, each captured to a file BEFORE any pipe.
- `eslint --no-inline-config --format json` over the three changed files: 0 errors. The 58 + 2 warnings it reports are pre-existing `no-explicit-any` hits in helpers this change does not touch; the diff adds none.
- Every heavy run went through the container's shared verify lock under one stable slot name, and each verdict above is that wrapper's own `VERDICT command-exit` line, ⛔ never a bare exit status read through a pipe.

## Acceptance notes

- Serial constraint re-taken immediately before my first write: all 16 open PRs enumerated (release PR included) and each one's file list read — zero touch `packages/plugin-form/src`. Re-taken, ⛔ not inherited from the claim comment.
- The diff reaches one file outside the dispatched surface: the member-pin ledger prose in `apps/console`, for the reason in the sweep section. It is one string literal inside a test; no published behaviour of `@object-ui/console` changes.
- `Refs`, not the closing keyword, on purpose: the card's own repro and its judgement are discharged, but the card states the drop in general terms and the headingless shape above still drops the key. The seat owns whether that shape is this card or a new one; ⛔ I did not close the card from here, and ⛔ I filed nothing.
- Out of scope, ⛔ not filed, reported in my hand-back: the `drawer` arm drops the same key at `DrawerForm`'s own divider push (reproducible, measured above); the headingless-section boundary; and the card's own arm table, which says five arms render the key when four do.
- Draft, as dispatched. ⛔ Not flipped ready, ⛔ not enqueued, ⛔ no label written by me.
